commits.message:
ESC ], P or _ opens a reply only while an ask awaits one, and is Alt on its key otherwise (rich-control-codes-xh4n.re6)

The parser asks its sink whether an ask is in flight. With none, an
unterminated control string is Alt+], Alt+P or Alt+_ at once, so keys typed
after it in one read are not held. With one, a reply split across slow reads
or right after its ESC is held until it ends, and the ask's timeout flushes
what was held. A terminated control string is a reply either way.

A running App asks its terminal; terminalColors reads OSC 10/11 (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk) (#538)

* A running App asks its terminal, and terminalColors reads its real foreground and background (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

The input parser reads OSC, DCS and APC strings and private-prefix CSI
reports as TerminalReply, never as keys. App.ask writes queries then DA1
and ends answered on DA1's reply, on a timeout, or when the app leaves;
App holds raw mode and the one reader, so the ask adds neither.
terminalColors asks OSC 10/11 and app.terminal draws the next frame on
the answer.

* A timed-out ask's late replies reach no later ask, a throwing ask leaves the queue running, and rgba: replies are read (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

* An ask whose write throws leaves nothing in flight, and a timeout must be positive and finite (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

* A reply split after its ESC is heard as one, an ask after the app stopped ends left, and the app builds its console one way (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)

* A held ESC before ], P or _ is Escape again, as rich-host-input-0c4f made it; the split-reply case waits on xh4n.re6 (rich-control-codes-xh4n.3xk)
